function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

Here’s a quick rundown of the most common tools, platforms, and APIs you’ll find useful when you’re looking to book flights—whether you’re building a travel app, automating a booking workflow, or just researching options:

| Category | Tool / Service | What it does | Typical use case |
|----------|----------------|--------------|------------------|
| **Flight Search & Booking APIs** | **Skyscanner API** | Aggregates flight prices from many airlines and travel agencies. Offers search, price alerts, and booking via partner links. | Building a price‑comparison widget or a “find cheapest flight” feature. |
| | **Google Flights API (via Google Travel)** | Provides flight availability, pricing, and itinerary details. Requires OAuth for booking. | Integrating Google’s flight search into your own UI or providing a Google‑powered search experience. |
| | **Amadeus Self‑Service APIs** | Includes flight offers, booking, and itinerary management. Supports dynamic pricing and seat selection. | Enterprise travel solutions, corporate booking portals, or travel agencies needing full control over bookings. |
| | **Kiwi.com API** | Known for “magic combinations” – combining multiple carriers into one ticket. Handles complex itineraries. | Offering unique multi‑carrier itineraries or “best‑price” guarantees. |
| | **Travelport Universal API** | Legacy but still widely used in B2B travel agencies. Covers flights, hotels, car rentals, etc. | Large travel agencies or OTAs that need a single point of integration for all travel products. |
| | **AirLabs API** | Real‑time flight status, delays, and historical data. | Adding live flight status updates or delay predictions to your booking flow. |
| | **OpenSky Network API** | Free real‑time flight tracking data. | Providing live flight tracking or visualizing flight paths in your app. |
| | **FlightAware API** | Flight status, arrival/departure times, and historical data. | Similar to OpenSky but more commercial‑grade and reliable for production use. |
| | **FlightStats API** | Detailed flight status, airport info, and weather. | Enhancing booking pages with accurate arrival/departure times and weather forecasts. |
| | **Sabre APIs** | Comprehensive travel solution covering flights, hotels, car rentals, and more. | Enterprise travel portals or large OTA integrations. |
| | **Cleartrip API** | Indian market focus, includes flights, hotels, and holiday packages. | Targeting the Indian travel market or building a localized booking portal. |
| | **Expedia Rapid API** | Access to Expedia’s inventory and booking engine. | Building a travel aggregator or integrating Expedia’s inventory into your own site. |
| | **Priceline Partner Network API** | Access to Priceline’s inventory and booking capabilities. | Building a travel agency platform that uses Priceline’s inventory. |
| | **Booking.com API** | Primarily hotels, but also offers flight booking via partner integrations. | Adding flight booking to a hotel‑centric travel site. |
| | **Trip.com API** | Global travel platform offering flights, hotels, trains, and more. | Building a global travel portal with a unified booking experience. |
| | **CheapOair API** | Focuses on discounted airfare and package deals. | Offering budget‑friendly flight options or last‑minute deals. |
| | **Kayak API** | Aggregates flight prices from many sources. | Building a price‑comparison tool or a “search across many sites” feature. |
| | **Momondo API** | Aggregates flight prices and offers price alerts. | Similar to Kayak – price comparison and alert features. |
| | **Travelpayouts API** | Affiliate network for flight, hotel, and car rental commissions. | Monetizing flight searches via affiliate links. |
| | **Skiplagged API** | Finds hidden‑city flight tickets and cheaper routes. | Offering alternative routing options or “hidden‑city” deals. |
| | **OpenFlights API** | Free database of airports, airlines, and routes. | Building custom flight maps or visualizations. |
| | **FlightRadar24 API** | Live flight tracking and historical data. | Adding live flight tracking widgets or dashboards. |
| | **FlightAware Firehose** | Real‑time flight data stream (paid). | Building high‑frequency flight monitoring or analytics dashboards. |
| | **FlightStats Firehose** | Real‑time flight status feed (paid). | Similar to FlightAware Firehose for real‑time analytics. |
| | **FlightHub API** | Aggregates flight inventory from many suppliers. | Building a travel aggregator or marketplace. |

### How to pick the right one

| Decision factor | What to look for | Example choice |
|-----------------|------------------|----------------|
| **Geographic focus** | Some APIs have better coverage in certain regions (e.g., Cleartrip for India, Skiplagged for hidden‑city deals). | Use Cleartrip if you’re targeting Indian travelers. |
| **Pricing model** | Pay‑per‑request vs. subscription. | Choose Amadeus or Travelport if you need enterprise‑level volume and support. |
| **Complexity of itineraries** | Multi‑stop, multi‑carrier, or “magic combination” itineraries. | Kiwi.com or Amadeus for complex itineraries. |
| **Affiliate / commission** | If you want to earn from bookings. | Travelpayouts or Skiplagged for affiliate revenue. |
| **Real‑time flight status** | Need live status or delay predictions. | FlightAware or FlightStats for real‑time data. |
| **Ease of integration** | REST vs. SOAP, SDKs available. | Skyscanner or Amadeus offer modern REST APIs with SDKs. |
| **Cost** | Some APIs charge per request or per booking. | Skyscanner is free for search but charges for booking. |

### Quick start checklist

1. **Define your scope** – Are you building a simple price‑comparison widget or a full OTA?  
2. **Choose a primary flight search API** – e.g., Skyscanner for quick prototyping, Amadeus for enterprise.  
3. **Add a booking layer** – Many search APIs redirect to partner booking pages; if you need direct booking, use Amadeus or Travelport.  
4. **Integrate flight status** – Add FlightAware or FlightStats for live updates.  
5. **Add affiliate tracking** – Use Travelpayouts or Skiplagged if you want to monetize.  
6. **Test with real data** – Use sandbox environments where available (Amadeus, Travelport).
